backlog.spec: Make LABEL_SMOOTHING a per-step value that decays linearly from its current 0.09 to 0 over the training steps, using the existing step counter. Inside forward_step, pass the current smoothing as a Python float argument, or keep it as a 0-dim tensor to avoid recompilation. Predict and the rest of the loop are unchanged.
backlog.title: Label smoothing annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Multiply the Muon group lr by a linear warmup factor min(1, (step+1)/W) with W about 3% of total_train_steps, combined with the existing linear-to-zero decay. Apply it in the same place where lr_factor2 is set in the training loop, leaving the SGD groups unchanged.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup for Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Change WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 0.0 or 0.05 so that the whitening bias is trained only briefly. Alternatively, freeze the whitening bias for the whole run. This is a one-constant change that removes the whiten-bias gradient path for most steps.
backlog.title: Shorter whitening-bias phase

backlog.spec: Replace the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) in CifarNet.layers with nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1) (or mean over spatial dims), so the spatial map is averaged before the head. Keep the head input size at 256 and keep the head scaling line consistent with the new feature count. This is a small architecture change that may trade a little speed for accuracy.
backlog.title: Global average pooling instead of final MaxPool(3)

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, after conv2 and norm2 and before the final SiLU, add the input of conv2 back to its output (x = x + residual) for the blocks where channels match. For block1 use a 1x1 projection or skip the residual. This adds identity paths around the second convolution and needs no new hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Residual connection inside each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Add a single learnable scalar parameter (initialised to 1, no weight decay, trained with the head SGD group) that multiplies the head output in CifarNet.forward, in place of the fixed division only by feature count. This lets the network set its logit temperature rather than relying on the fixed scale.
backlog.title: Learnable scalar multiplier on the head output

backlog.spec: Replace the linear head with a classifier that L2-normalises the 256-dim features and the 10 class weight vectors and multiplies the cosine by a fixed scale of about 8 to 16. Keep the head trained by the head SGD group and the label-smoothing loss. This changes the output geometry without changing the conv trunk.
backlog.title: Cosine-style normalized classifier head

backlog.spec: Change widths to block1=96, block2=256, block3=192 or a similar shift of capacity. Keep the rest of the network and the Muon setup the same. Check that the parameter count and the Newton-Schulz padding (max_D, max_K) are still computed from the new shapes.
backlog.title: Wider first block with narrower last block

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the conv and head weights during training, with decay about 0.99 to 0.998 updated after each optimizer step. At the end of train(), copy the EMA weights into the model used by predict. BatchNorm running stats should be copied from the same EMA or recalculated. The EMA is created inside train() so no state survives between runs.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights for prediction

backlog.spec: During the last 25% of training steps, accumulate a running average of the conv weights (a uniform average of snapshots taken every few steps). Load the average into the model at the end of train(). Snapshots are taken after the optimizer step, and the average buffer is allocated inside train() each run.
backlog.title: Averaging of late-training iterates

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz iterations in _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 from 3 to 2, or increase it to 4 if the result looks unstable. This is a direct change to the three unrolled blocks, and it trades orthogonalisation accuracy for step time. The coefficients a, b, c stay the same.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: Group the filter tensors by identical reshaped (D, K) shape before padding, so that the Newton-Schulz batch is split into a few uniform stacks instead of one padded stack. This reduces wasted FLOPs on padding when block1 (K=27 or 24) and block2/3 (K=2304) are padded to the same max_K. Only the internal stacking code of Muon changes.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz on each channel group in a single batched call

backlog.spec: Set nesterov=False for the Muon optimizer (the second optimizer) and keep the other settings. This drops the extra foreach_add for the nesterov buffer. Test whether accuracy holds at the same epoch count, since the momentum schedule was tuned with Nesterov on.
backlog.title: Nesterov off for Muon

backlog.spec: Replace the epoch-alternating flip in CifarLoader with a per-sample random flip applied every epoch, using the existing batch_flip_lr compiled helper on each batch (or on the full pre-normalised tensor once per epoch). Keep the translation and jitter as they are.
backlog.title: Per-sample random horizontal flip instead of alternating epochs

backlog.spec: For the first ~30% of epochs, downscale the training images to 24x24 with area interpolation (F.interpolate, cheap) before the pad and crop step, then switch to 32x32 for the remaining epochs. Compiled forward_step will recompile once for the new shape, which happens during the untimed warm-up only if shapes are fixed, so keep the two shapes fixed across runs. Predict stays at 32x32.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution with downscaled early epochs

backlog.spec: Start training with batch size 768 and grow it to 1536 in two or three steps across training, keeping the per-step learning rates scaled by the batch ratio so the effective step size is similar. Each batch size needs a fixed shape to avoid repeated compilation, so restrict the steps to two or three sizes. Update the loader's batch size and the step count accordingly.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp

backlog.spec: Apply a random 8x8 zero-out (cutout) to about 30% of images in each batch after normalisation, using a random centre for each image, implemented with a compiled mask helper. Applying the same mask to all channels is enough. This is an additional augmentation with no new hyperparameters beyond the mask size and probability.
backlog.title: Cutout regulariser on a fraction of the batch

backlog.spec: Add nn.Dropout with p=0.1 on the 256-dim feature vector before the head Linear, active only during training. Predict remains in eval mode so it is unaffected. This is a small regulariser that may help a model trained for about 8 epochs or may hurt, so test it with one replicate.
backlog.title: Dropout before the head

backlog.spec: In infer's tta function, raise the uncertainty quantile UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE from 0.25 to 1.0 so that all test images receive the shifted and flipped views. Compare the accuracy gain against the added prediction time. Keep the same two crops and the flip.
backlog.title: Denser TTA over more of the test set

backlog.spec: Add two more shifted views to the TTA views in _get_tta_logits, for example the (0,2) and (2,0) corners from the reflect-padded images, so that the averaged logits use five translations and their flips. The output stays a mean over views. Compile shape stays fixed because the number of views is constant.
backlog.title: Extra shifted views in TTA

backlog.spec: Reduce the color jitter to brightness only, or contrast only, on alternate epochs, or apply jitter to half of each batch. This tests whether the current combined jitter at 0.14 and 0.13 is more than the short schedule needs. The change is in the aug dictionary and the batch_color_jitter call, not the optimiser.
backlog.title: Mixed per-batch brightness and contrast jitter with a cap

backlog.spec: Change whiten_kernel_size from 2 to 3 in CifarNet, which makes the fixed patch-statistics whitening convolution produce a larger number of channels (2*3*9 = 54). The whiten_width used by ConvGroup1 follows automatically. init_whiten already uses the kernel shape, so only the constant changes, but check the shape of the output map after padding.
backlog.title: Whitening layer with kernel size 3

backlog.spec: Store the per-group learning rates as 0-dim CUDA tensors and update them with a single fill or in-place copy each step, instead of setting Python floats in the optimizer param groups every iteration. Keep the optimizer step itself unchanged. This removes Python overhead from the roughly 1500 steps and should not change the results.
backlog.title: Reduce per-step Python overhead with precomputed LR tensors

backlog.spec: Change the forward_step compile decorator from mode='max-autotune' to mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' or test the reduce-overhead mode, which captures the forward and backward graph and removes launch overhead for batch 1536. Because compilation is untimed and cached, only the steady-state step time matters. Verify the shapes of the last partial batch are not an issue, since drop_last keeps the shape fixed.
backlog.title: CUDA graph mode for the forward step

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 1024 and scale the Muon and SGD learning rates, and the weight decay (which is scaled by batch size in train()), by about 2/3 to keep a comparable per-epoch update. This gives more optimizer steps per epoch which may help the short schedule. Check the number of steps and the step-count rounding after the change.
backlog.title: Smaller batch with the learning rates rescaled

backlog.spec: Ramp MUON_MOMENTUM from about 0.5 up to 0.655 (or to 0.85 then down) over the first 10% of steps, using a simple linear factor on the group's momentum value that is applied before the Muon step. This prevents early momentum overshoot while the network is still learning the whitened features.
backlog.title: Larger Muon momentum warm-start

backlog.spec: Replace the linear-to-zero decay used for the SGD groups (biases, norms and head) with a cosine decay to zero over total_train_steps, leaving the Muon learning rate on its linear decay. This mixes two schedule shapes, tests whether the head and bias learning rate benefit from a slower tail.
backlog.title: Cosine decay for SGD bias and head learning rates

backlog.spec: Set weight_decay to zero for the norm bias group in param_configs, keeping the whiten bias and head decay as they are. Weight decay on the BatchNorm biases is small but the group is tiny, so this just removes an unneeded term. It is a one-line change in the param_configs construction.
backlog.title: Remove the per-group weight decay on norm biases

backlog.spec: Extend the existing low-res schedule into three stages. For the first 15% of total_train_steps, downscale each batch with F.interpolate(size=(16,16), mode='area'). From 15% to 45%, use size (24,24). After that, use the native 32x32. Keep the rest of train() unchanged, including the whiten-init on full-resolution images and the forward_step compile. Compute the stage boundaries from total_train_steps, and keep the forward_step compile as is, accepting a recompile per shape. If recompiles are costly, mark the stage input shapes as dynamic=False or pre-warm them in the untimed call.
backlog.title: Three-stage progressive resolution (16, 24, 32)

backlog.spec: Use a bigger batch while the input is downscaled, for example 3072 for the first 30% of steps, then 1536 for the rest. Each stage's Muon and SGD learning rates are scaled by sqrt(new_batch/1536) at that stage, and weight decay is scaled with the batch as the script already does. Split the loader into stages, or re-batch the same permutation with a stage-dependent batch size. Keep len(train_loader)-based step counting consistent by computing total_train_steps from the sample count, so the total epoch budget is unchanged.
backlog.title: Larger batch during the low-resolution phase

backlog.spec: Keep a per-sample loss buffer of size 50000 that lives inside the train() call only, so it is not reused across runs. Record each sample's per-example cross-entropy (reduction='none') during the training forward pass. From epoch 3 onward, each epoch skips the 15% of samples with the lowest recorded loss from the previous epoch. Sample the remaining indices with the existing randperm. Scale the number of steps per epoch accordingly so the total step count stays the same, and keep the loss normalisation by batch size as it is now.
backlog.title: Drop the easiest samples from later epochs

backlog.spec: Replace the nn.MaxPool2d(2) in ConvGroup with a fixed mix pool(x) = 0.5*MaxPool2d(2)(x) + 0.5*AvgPool2d(2)(x). Both are parameter-free, so there is no change to the optimizer groups or to the Muon meta data. The final nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) stays as it is. Check that the mix is channels_last compatible and runs in half precision, and keep the BatchNorm after the pool as it is now.
backlog.title: Blend max and average pooling in ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Swap the nn.SiLU() activations inside ConvGroup for a squared-SiLU, activ(x) = SiLU(x) * relu(x) / (something bounded), or more simply x -> SiLU(x)**2 with the sign kept, for example sign(x)*SiLU(|x|)**2. Keep the activation fused in the compiled graph and do not add learned parameters. Batch norm without learned scale is kept as it is, so the post-norm activation scale stays near unity. The head scaling by 1/x.size(-1) is unchanged.
backlog.title: Squared SiLU activation in place of SiLU

backlog.spec: In the Muon step, multiply each filter's orthogonalised update by max(1, rows/cols)**0.5, where rows and cols are the reshaped (D, K) dimensions of that filter. This is the usual shape-dependent scale used in Muon implementations, and it changes only a scalar per filter. Compute the factor once in __init__ from filter_params_meta and store it in a list, so no new torch.compile graph is needed. Keep the Newton-Schulz function and the padding logic unchanged, so the compile path that crashed earlier is not touched.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon update scale

backlog.spec: Change the Muon learning-rate schedule from linear to quadratic decay: lr_t = MUON_LR * (1 - p)**2, where p = step/total_train_steps. Apply the same change to the target_magnitude interpolation inside the Newton-Schulz function, keeping its endpoint values the same. The SGD bias and head learning rates stay linear. Only the lr_factor2 computation in the training loop and the progress ratio are affected.
backlog.title: Quadratic decay for the Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Insert nn.Dropout2d(p=0.1) after the activation at the end of the first ConvGroup (block1 output), active only in train mode. Use nn.Dropout2d because it drops whole channels, which suits the convolutional features. The model is in eval mode during predict, so inference is unaffected. Keep the dropout module inside the existing CifarNet so make_model is unchanged. Note that model.half() and channels_last are applied after construction, so the dropout layer needs no special handling.
backlog.title: Spatial dropout after the first block

backlog.spec: In predict(), before running the model, bilinearly upsample the normalised test images by a factor of 1.1 (about 35px), using F.interpolate with align_corners=False. Run the existing TTA path on the upscaled images, and keep the reflect-pad shifted views and flip averaging as they are, with the pad scaled to the new size. Do not change the model or its state, and do not use test labels. This tests whether the train-time augmentation scale mismatch can be reduced at inference.
backlog.title: FixRes-style test-time upscaling in predict

backlog.spec: Set nesterov=False in the torch.optim.SGD call that creates optimizer1, so the bias, norm-bias, and head updates use plain momentum. Keep SGD_MOMENTUM and the learning-rate schedule unchanged. The Muon optimizer keeps its own Nesterov setting. This is a one-line change that tests whether the classical momentum form is better for the small-scale parameters at this short schedule.
backlog.title: Nesterov off for the SGD bias and head optimizer

backlog.spec: In CifarNet, replace nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) at the end of self.layers with nn.Flatten(), so the head sees all 256 channels at each of the 4x4 spatial positions (4096 inputs). Change self.head to nn.Linear(256*4*4, 10, bias=False). In forward, remove the x.view(len(x), -1) pooling dependence and keep the existing /x.size(-1) head scaling, which now divides by 4096, so also check that the head LR and the reset() rescaling of head weights still give sensible logit scale. Keep the low-res phase working by making the head input size depend on the resolution, or by only using the flatten path at full 32x32 and max pooling during the 24x24 phase.
backlog.title: Flatten the final 4x4 map into the head instead of global max pooling

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, drop the nn.MaxPool2d(2) layer and make conv1 a strided convolution with stride 2 and padding 1 (kernel 3) so it downsamples 2x while mapping channels_in to channels_out. Reorder the forward so it is conv1 (stride 2), norm1, activation, conv2, norm2, activation. Keep the Conv class's dirac initialisation for the non-strided case in mind: for the strided conv, initialise with the same dirac pattern on the first channels only if shapes allow, otherwise use the default init. The rest of the pipeline (whitening, low-res 24x24 phase, Muon) is unchanged. This tests whether a learned downsample beats fixed max pooling at this tiny budget.
backlog.title: Strided 3x3 convolution replaces max pooling in each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: At the end of train(), before returning, set the model to train mode with no gradient, reset every BatchNorm running_mean and running_var (or set BN momentum to None for cumulative averaging), and run a forward pass over a fixed set of about 10000 un-augmented training images (normalised, no flip, no translation, no colour jitter) in batches of 2000, so the BN running statistics match the clean test distribution rather than the jittered training distribution. Then call model.eval(). Only data already given to train() is used, so this respects the run-from-scratch rule. Cost is a few forward passes, well under 0.1 s.
backlog.title: Train-mode BatchNorm recalibration on clean images after training

backlog.spec: Inside train(), keep a per-sample loss vector of length 50000 that starts at zero and is updated after each training step with the per-sample cross entropy of the batch (compute the unreduced loss from the forward output, detached). Each epoch after the first, draw the permutation as torch.multinomial over per-sample weights proportional to the stored loss (plus a floor of 0.2 of the mean so easy samples still appear), sampling without replacement across the epoch. Keep the number of steps per epoch unchanged. The stored loss vector is created inside train() each run, so no data carries across runs. Implement it by overriding the randperm line in CifarLoader.__iter__ via a weights argument, keeping the flip and translation logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Loss-weighted hard example sampling across epochs

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform randperm shuffle in CifarLoader.__iter__ with a class-stratified order: for each epoch, shuffle the indices of each of the 10 classes separately, then interleave them so every consecutive block of BATCH_SIZE contains roughly 153 samples from each class (round-robin across classes, then shuffle within the batch). Since CIFAR-10 is balanced this changes little in expectation but removes batch-to-batch label-count variance, which may reduce gradient noise in the BatchNorm statistics. Build the class index lists inside train() from the labels argument each run, not from any cached state.
backlog.title: Stratified class-balanced batches

backlog.spec: In the training loop, for 25 percent of batches after the first 20 percent of steps, apply CutMix: sample a Beta(1,1) lambda, draw a random permutation of the batch, cut a rectangle of side sqrt(1-lambda)*32 at a random location from the permuted batch and paste it into the original batch, then recompute lambda from the actual pasted area. The loss is lambda * CE(out, y) + (1-lambda) * CE(out, y_perm), with the label smoothing setting kept. Use the same forward_step with the mixed inputs; the loss is a sum, so keep the reduction as is. The 24x24 low-res phase should apply CutMix after the interpolate. This is a regulariser that trades fit speed for generalisation, so it may be net negative at 7.65 epochs, which is the point of the test.
backlog.title: CutMix on a fraction of batches with soft targets

backlog.spec: Replace optimizer1 (torch.optim.SGD with Nesterov momentum over the whiten bias, norm biases and head) with torch.optim.AdamW using the same parameter groups, base learning rates BIAS_LR for the bias groups and HEAD_LR for the head, betas (0.9, 0.99), and weight decay set so that the decoupled decay equals the current effective decay (wd / lr). Keep the linear decay of each group's lr to zero using the existing lr_factor logic, which multiplies initial_lr. Because Adam's update magnitude is not proportional to the gradient, the learning rates may need to be divided by roughly 10 to 20; try BIAS_LR scaled by 0.05 and HEAD_LR scaled by 0.05 as the first setting. Muon stays unchanged.
backlog.title: AdamW for the whitening bias, norm biases and head in place of Nesterov SGD

backlog.spec: Replace the linear decay of the Muon learning rate (lr_factor2 = 1 - step/total_train_steps for optimizer2) with a trapezoid: hold the factor at 1.0 for the first 40 percent of total_train_steps, then decay linearly to 0 at the final step. Implement it as lr_factor2 = min(1.0, (1 - step/total_train_steps) / 0.6). Apply the same trapezoid to the SGD head and bias groups, or keep those linear, as a separate choice. Leave the Muon target magnitude schedule inside the Newton-Schulz function unchanged so no compiled code is affected. This tests whether a longer high-LR plateau followed by a fast anneal helps a short run.
backlog.title: Trapezoidal learning-rate schedule for Muon

backlog.spec: Extend batch_color_jitter with a saturation jitter: for each image, draw a saturation factor s in [1-0.15, 1+0.15] and blend each pixel with its per-image grayscale value (mean over channels, computed on the normalised tensor as a per-image channel mean) as out = gray + s*(x - gray). Additionally, with probability 0.1 per image, replace the image by its grayscale version. Keep brightness and contrast jitter as they are. Apply these inside the same torch.compile'd function, so no extra Python overhead is added. This is a data-side change that adds colour diversity without touching the network.
backlog.title: Per-channel saturation and random grayscale augmentation

backlog.spec: Let the head weight (shape 10 by 256, currently handled by the SGD optimizer) join the Muon group. In the Muon constructor and in train(), add the head weight to the 2D path by reshaping it to a 4D tensor of shape (10, 256, 1, 1) before the Newton-Schulz step, or by extending the meta tuple to handle 2D parameters with reshaped_D=10 and reshaped_K=256; keep max_D and max_K as they are so the compiled Newton-Schulz function sees the same padded shapes, which avoids the recompile crashes seen earlier. Remove the head from param_configs in optimizer1. Use a head learning rate equal to MUON_LR times the current ratio of HEAD_LR to the Muon LR, and keep the weight decay of the head unchanged. The aim is a better-conditioned head update.
backlog.title: Muon also orthogonalises the classifier head

incumbent.description: Train on 24x24 area-downscaled batches for the first 30% of steps, then 32x32, with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so the 24x24 path (2x2 map at the last pool) doesn't break the head; predict stays at 32x32.

memo:
Helped: only a data/resolution change. Slot 1 (24x24 area-downscaled batches for the first 30% of steps, then 32x32) is the sole accept, with runs at -0.1496 and -0.0840 and mean adjusted -0.1141. It carries a tripwire flag, so replicate or audit it before building on it.

Did not help: extra TTA views (+0.0134 vs incumbent), label smoothing annealed to 0 (+0.0098), Muon LR warmup (+0.0610), alternating jitter (+0.0178), Nesterov off for SGD (+0.0081) or Muon (+0.1991), batch-size ramp (+0.3290), gradient accumulation in low-res phase (+0.2084), three-stage resolution (+0.0773), AdamW (+0.8563), whitening kernel 3 (+0.2957), identity skip (+0.1130). Class-stratified shuffle was roughly neutral (-0.0040). Slots 3 and 4 crashed from torch.compile on per-shape Newton-Schulz changes.

Next: replicate slot 1 first. Then try small variations of the low-res fraction or size (for example a different fraction than 30%, or a size other than 24). Avoid compile-fragile Muon edits. Single-number tuning, TTA and optimizer-flag tweaks look low-yield.
